title: The Promotion Trap
subtitle: From middle management to the executive floor
description: Five corporate crises. Four deeply suspicious metrics. One promotion you absolutely do not deserve.

stages.title: The Productivity Crisis
stages.text: Your team has finished its work ahead of schedule. Senior management is worried this means they have too much spare time. Your director wants to see decisive leadership.

options.label: Introduce compulsory daily progress meetings.
options.title: Communication has never been stronger.
options.text: Productivity drops. Meeting attendance hits 100%. You receive a leadership award for improving alignment.

options.label: Reduce headcount to capture efficiency savings.
options.title: A leaner, meaner disaster.
options.text: The remaining team is overwhelmed. Finance applauds your cost discipline. Nobody asks whether the work still gets done.

options.label: Raise every target by 40%.
options.title: Ambition successfully deployed.
options.text: Your best employees resign. HR calls this an exciting opportunity to refresh the talent pipeline.

options.label: Explain that a high-performing team is a good thing.
options.title: An uncomfortable commitment to reality.
options.text: The team appreciates your support. Your director questions whether you have the hunger required for senior leadership.

stages.speaker: sven

stages.title: The Morale Emergency
stages.text: The staff survey says morale is collapsing because of excessive meetings, impossible deadlines and poor management. HR recommends an urgent, highly visible intervention.

options.label: Run a compulsory half-day resilience workshop.
options.title: Resilience achieved. Allegedly.
options.text: Employees lose another half-day to meetings. Attendance is perfect, which HR reports as overwhelming support.

options.label: Establish a Culture Champions Committee.
options.title: A committee is born.
options.text: Twelve people are volunteered without being asked. The committee schedules a meeting to define its purpose.

options.label: Announce free pizza on Friday.
options.title: A slice of transformation.
options.text: Staff eat the pizza. The CEO describes your initiative as a breakthrough in employee experience.

options.label: Cancel unnecessary meetings and adjust workloads.
options.title: A suspiciously practical solution.
options.text: Morale improves. Your boss wants to know why you did not launch a formal programme with a logo.

stages.speaker: janice

stages.title: The Innovation Mandate
stages.text: The CEO wants every division to demonstrate measurable innovation by Friday. Nobody has defined innovation. The executive team has already ordered branded lanyards.

options.label: Create an Innovation Steering Committee.
options.title: Governance is innovation.
options.text: Six meetings are booked. The committee produces a logo, a charter and no innovations whatsoever.

options.label: Require three ideas from every employee.
options.title: Ideation at scale.
options.text: Four hundred ideas are submitted. None are read. The participation dashboard is a glorious shade of green.

options.label: Rebrand the existing workflow as AI-enabled.
options.title: The future is now. Again.
options.text: Nothing changes except the slide deck. The CEO calls your division a digital pioneer.

options.label: Give employees time to test useful ideas.
options.title: Innovation accidentally occurs.
options.text: Two valuable improvements emerge. Finance wants to know why staff were not doing their regular jobs.

stages.speaker: brad

stages.title: The Incident Report
stages.text: A customer has found a serious error in a report your division approved. Your director asks for an update before the board meeting in twenty minutes.

options.label: Rename the error an “emerging opportunity”.
options.title: Narrative successfully controlled.
options.text: The board congratulates you on your positive framing. The customer remains furious, but they were not invited to the meeting.

options.label: Create a working group to investigate ownership.
options.title: Accountability has been distributed.
options.text: Seven departments now share responsibility. This is functionally indistinguishable from nobody having responsibility.

options.label: Publish a dashboard showing 99% report accuracy.
options.title: The numbers speak for themselves.
options.text: You exclude the faulty report as an outlier. The dashboard is green. The problem is not.

options.label: Own the mistake and tell the customer how it will be fixed.
options.title: A regrettable outbreak of integrity.
options.text: The customer stays. The team learns something. Your director says you have made the situation unnecessarily visible.

stages.speaker: sarah

stages.title: The Final Promotion
stages.text: The organisation is in turmoil. The CEO needs a new Chief Transformation Officer to lead a company-wide turnaround. You have five minutes to make your pitch.

options.label: Promise a bold transformation roadmap with seven workstreams.
options.title: The roadmap is the destination.
options.text: The CEO is impressed by your ambition. A consultant is hired to explain what the workstreams mean.

options.label: Blame legacy culture and propose a complete restructure.
options.title: The future requires fewer witnesses.
options.text: Your predecessor is blamed. Three layers of management are added to make the organisation flatter.

options.label: Present a glossy dashboard of all your achievements.
options.title: Presentation is everything.
options.text: Every metric is green because you designed the metrics. The CEO is delighted by your evidence-based approach.

options.label: Describe the problems honestly and propose achievable fixes.
options.title: You may have misunderstood the assignment.
options.text: Your plan would probably work. The board worries you lack the visionary mindset required to lead transformation.

stages.speaker: richard
